Subject: Re: High tail latency after runtime bump (Lachlan Labs on-prem)

Olga,

We're seeing a sustained p95/p99 latency increase and a ~15% throughput drop on our on-prem cluster since we applied the 'v3-kernel' runtime update last night. Error spikes (HTTP 503) correlate with bursts of longer traces — attached is a short summary (request_summaries.csv) and a tail-sample.

Symptoms: 
- Intermittent 503s from the inference endpoint during steady traffic (~2k rps).
- p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms, p99 to ~1.8s.
- Throughput down ~15% vs baseline; CPU/GPU utilization unchanged.
- We rolled model variant back for one node; that node's latencies improved but cluster-level problem persisted.

We suspect something in the runtime change interacting with our NUMA layout / batch window. Can your eng team triage? This is impacting our customer-facing SLA; Cam (CTO) is on-copy.

Thanks,
Sarah Park
Head of Production
Lachlan Labs

Subject: Re: High tail latency after runtime bump (triage & immediate mitigations)

Sarah — thanks for the signal and the sample data. We're treating this as Priority 1. I've looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Marcus (runtime) to triage.

Immediate steps we recommend this morning (safe to apply with small risk):
- Enable inbound model-fallback: we can pin production route to prior runtime variant for 10% of traffic as a targeted canary.
- Temporarily disable the new opportunistic queue suppression flag on the on-prem agents (opportunistic_queue_suppression=false).
- Increase max-inflight per-server by +2 and shrink batch window from 7ms -> 3ms to reduce tail batching.

Marcus will push a tuning patch + a short runbook you can apply; if that doesn't get p95 back under control we'll schedule a controlled rollback/canary this evening and an exec sync with Cam.

I'll be standing by on Slack and can join a call.

From: marcus.lin@redwood.example

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High tail latency after runtime bump (initial analysis + config patch)

Sarah / Olga — I pulled the logs and the kernel traces you sent. Quick summary of what I see and a low-risk tuning patch attached (kernel_tuning_patch.diff):

Observations:
- The new kernel's opportunistic queue suppression is batching across NUMA boundaries under your topology; that increases stray queue wait time for a subset of requests (p99).
- Continuous batching combined with a slightly larger default batch-window (7ms) amplifies tail latencies under bursty traffic.
- KV-cache warmup looks fine; not a cache-miss issue.

Recommended immediate actions (safe & reversible):
1) Set opportunistic_queue_suppression=false across on-prem agent config (rollout group: 10% -> 30% -> 100% if good).
2) Reduce batch_window_ms from 7 to 3 for real-time routes.
3) Pin worker threads to socket-local cores (example: taskset mask provided in patch).
4) If rolling these changes is operationally heavy, we can run a targeted canary rollback to the prior runtime variant for up to 20% of traffic.

Commands and patch are attached (kernel_tuning_patch.diff). I added a short health-check script to monitor p95/p99 and 503 rate. Please run the script in /tmp on your agents and paste the output.

I'll be available for a live run-through.

- Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
marcus.lin@redwood.example

At this point we're evaluating two options: a) full canary rollback to the previous runtime across the whole cluster during low traffic window, or b) a staged canary to prior runtime with incremental traffic shift (10/30/100). We'd like Redwood to run the rollback plan with us — we need an ops owner in the call.

Also want to flag potential contractual impact; I'll escalate to our procurement team if we see more customer impact tomorrow. Can we schedule a 30-minute exec sync (Cam + Sarah + Redwood exec/CS) first thing Monday?
